newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates seen slipping further.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates seen slipping further.

text.p: Dutch money rates eased somewhat on Wednesday as nervousness on the direction of rates faded and dealers said guilder rates could slip a little further.
They said Tuesday's German industrial orders data, the success of Russian president Yeltsin's heart surgery and U.S. president Clinton's re-election had given the market a break.
"Upward pressure has faded and rates are not expected to rise in the near-term. This as long as we're not caught by any surprise," said one dealer.
The friendly sentiment in the capital market also supported lower rates in the money market.
But, call money rates were edging up nearer the loans rate which the central bank offers to commercial banks under the special advances pact. The pact is currently set at 2.50 percent.
Yesterday call money fell substantially to a bid range of 2.25-2.50 percent as the extra advances pact on top of the regular facility was covering the market with liquidity.

Last Friday, the central bank decided on an extra pact as the market fell short of liquidity, mainly because the state had stepped up its issuance of Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs), which absorbed quite a lot of liquidity.
Call money rose to 2.43-2.50 around midday.
Dealers said they expected overnight money to grade further after the central bank sets a new pact this afternoon at 1500 GMT.
The advances pact was seen remaining at 2.50 percent.
"The advances rate will rise, but there is no need yet," said one dealer.
Three-month deposits slipped two basis points to 2.90 percent bid.
The guilder was unchanged at 112.14 per 100 marks.
